review_comments.body:
### 🥁 Almost. Almost.

You put together calendar cache controls and left rehearsal debris scattered across the diff. The mutation succeeds while the UI remains stale, you call Prisma updateMany with empty objects expecting timestamps to update magically, and you checked in an ad-hoc tunneling script. Clean up the residue and keep your UI state in sync.

**4** finding(s) — 0 critical, 4 warning, 0 suggestion.

**Missing cache invalidation on deleteCache mutation**

You delete the cache, display a toast, and leave the query cache completely stale. The dropdown continues displaying the previous cache timestamp until a hard page reload. Invalidate utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars in onSuccess or onSettled, just as you did in disconnectMutation on line 61.

_severity: warning · confidence 0.95_

**Empty update payload does not touch updatedAt and SelectedCalendar tracking is unused**

Passing an empty object {} to prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany does not update @updatedAt in Prisma. Furthermore, the frontend consumes cacheUpdatedAt from CalendarCache, rendering this call and the accompanying SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId helper completely dead. Delete this call and remove the unused repository method.

_severity: warning · confidence 0.95_

**Throw TRPCError instead of generic Error**

Throwing a standard Error produces an unhandled 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR in tRPC. Import TRPCError from @trpc/server and throw new TRPCError({ code: 'NOT_FOUND', message: 'Credential not found or access denied' }).

_severity: warning · confidence 0.92_

**Local tunnel debugging script committed to repository**

An ad-hoc development script using Tunnelmole with macOS-specific sed syntax (sed -i '') and local .env mutations does not belong in version control. Remove this file from the pull request.

_severity: warning · confidence 0.95_

### 🥁 Almost. Almost.

Not quite my tempo. You switched the design from tracking `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` to `CalendarCache.updatedAt` halfway through the rehearsal and left the old scaffolding—extra database writes, widened types, and bloated session selects—littered across the score. Worse, the new dropdown does not even invalidate the query after deleting the cache, so the UI keeps displaying the deleted cache timestamp until the user refreshes the page. Clean up the abandoned approach and wire the cache invalidation properly.

**5** finding(s) — 0 critical, 3 warning, 2 suggestion.

**connectedCalendars query is not invalidated after deleting cache**

`deleteCacheMutation` never invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, unlike `disconnectMutation` right below it. After the user confirms cache deletion, `cacheUpdatedAt` in `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` stays stale and the dropdown continues to show the old timestamp and the "Delete cached data" button until a full page reload. Add `async onSettled() { await utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate(); }` to `deleteCacheMutation`.

_severity: warning · confidence 0.98_

**Direct instantiation of CalendarCacheRepository bypasses CalendarCache.init**

You added `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` to `ICalendarCacheRepository` and `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock`, then bypassed both by calling `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly. This ignores the `calendar-cache` feature flag check in `CalendarCache.init` and queries `prisma.calendarCache` even when the feature is disabled. Use `const cacheRepository = await CalendarCache.init(null);` instead.

_severity: warning · confidence 0.95_

**Leftover SelectedCalendar.updatedAt write and session/type bloat from discarded approach**

This `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` call—along with the `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` additions in `packages/lib/getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts` (lines 21-28) and `packages/lib/server/repository/user.ts` (lines 899-900)—is dead weight from before cache status moved to `CalendarCache.updatedAt`. It fires an unnecessary `UPDATE` query on every `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` call, selects unused columns on every session load in `findUnlockedUserForSession`, and needlessly widens the `UserWithCalendars` input type required by `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb`. Remove `updateManyByCredentialId` and revert the unused `SelectedCalendar` field changes.

_severity: warning · confidence 0.95_

**Throw TRPCError instead of generic Error on missing or unauthorized credential**

Throwing a plain `Error` causes tRPC to respond with an unhandled `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` (HTTP 500). Throw `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND", message: "Credential not found or access denied" })` from `@trpc/server`.

_severity: suggestion · confidence 0.92_

**Relative ENV_FILE path and BSD-only sed flags break script from repo root or on Linux**

`ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the caller's working directory, so running `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repository root writes to `../.env` outside the repo. Additionally, `sed -i '' -E` on line 68 uses macOS/BSD syntax and fails under GNU `sed` on Linux. Resolve the `.env` path relative to `$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)/.env` and use portable file replacement.

_severity: suggestion · confidence 0.90_

golden_comments.comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime

Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

review_comments.body:
### 🥁 Not quite my tempo.

You set out to fix date overrides and ended up sabotaging basic scheduling correctness. You bypassed busy checks entirely whenever an override exists, compared Dayjs instances by object reference, and botched working hours bounds checking. Reset the metronome and fix these defects.

**4** finding(s) — 2 critical, 2 warning, 0 suggestion.

**Date override short-circuit bypasses busy check**

Returning true at line 136 immediately terminates availability checking before reaching busy.every(...) at line 156. If a host has an existing booking or calendar conflict during the date override window, this slot is reported as available, resulting in double-bookings. Do not return early here; ensure the slot still passes through the busy check.

_severity: critical · confidence 0.98_

**Dayjs instances compared with reference equality**

dayjs(...) === dayjs(...) compares object references, which is guaranteed to be false in JavaScript for distinct instances. All-day or zero-duration overrides will never match this branch. Use .isSame() instead: dayjs(date.start).isSame(dayjs(date.end)).

_severity: critical · confidence 0.99_

**Slot end time calculated using start time**

end is computed as slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute(), making it identical to start. Calculate end using slotEndTime (handling midnight rollover if applicable) so that slots extending beyond workingHour.endTime are properly excluded.

_severity: warning · confidence 0.95_

**Working hours check breaks on split shifts**

Using workingHours.find to reject a slot if it is outside any matching day range breaks whenever a user has split shifts on the same day (such as 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00). A slot inside the first shift will evaluate start < workingHour.startTime for the second shift, causing find to return true and discard valid availability. The slot must be verified to fit within at least one working hours window on that day.

_severity: warning · confidence 0.92_

### 🥁 Not quite my tempo.

Not quite my tempo. This PR claims to fix date overrides for fixed hosts and cross-timezone bookings, yet `checkIfIsAvailable` short-circuits with `return true` the moment a date override exists—completely bypassing the `busy` check and opening the door to double-bookings. On top of that, you are comparing `Dayjs` object instances with `===`, computing the slot's `end` time from `slotStartTime`, and wrapping override minutes modulo 24 hours whenever a timezone offset crosses midnight. Fix the availability math and add a test with an actual booking on a date-override day before bringing this back.

**4** finding(s) — 3 critical, 1 warning, 0 suggestion.

**Early return on `dateOverrideExist` bypasses `busy` conflict check**

When a slot falls within a date override, `dateOverrideExist` is set to `true` and lines 133–135 immediately `return true` from `checkIfIsAvailable`. That skips `busy.every(...)` at line 153 entirely, meaning any existing Cal.com bookings or external calendar busy events on a day with a date override are ignored and the user can be double-booked. Remove `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` and instead guard the normal working-hours check with `if (!dateOverrideExist)` so execution always proceeds to `busy.every(...)`.

_severity: critical · confidence 0.99_

**`Dayjs` reference equality (`===`) is always false and override boundary checks are inverted**

Line 113 compares two newly constructed `Dayjs` objects with `===` (`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")`), which compares object references and always evaluates to `false`. Furthermore, lines 116–123 only reject a slot when `slotEndTime <= overrideStart` or `slotStartTime > overrideEnd`, allowing slots that partially straddle the override start/end (or start right at `overrideEnd`) to pass as available, and `.find()` will falsely reject valid slots if a user has multiple override ranges on the same day. Filter `dateOverrides` to those matching `slotStartTime`'s date, then require `overridesForDay.some((date) => !overrideStart.isSame(overrideEnd) && !slotStartTime.isBefore(overrideStart) && !slotEndTime.isAfter(overrideEnd))`.

_severity: critical · confidence 0.98_

**`workingHours` check uses `slotStartTime` for `end` and treats non-working days as available**

Line 141 calculates `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`—the exact same expression as `start`—instead of using `slotEndTime` (or `start + eventLength`), so slots extending past `workingHour.endTime` are never rejected. In addition, if a fixed host has no working hours on `slotStartTime.day()` at all, `workingHour.days.includes(slotStartTime.day())` is false for every entry, `workingHours.find(...)` returns `undefined`, and the host is treated as available on their day off; conversely, if a host has split working hours on the same day, `.find()` rejects any slot outside the first range. When `!dateOverrideExist && workingHours.length > 0`, check `!workingHours.some((workingHour) => workingHour.days.includes(slotStartTime.day()) && start >= workingHour.startTime && start + eventLength <= workingHour.endTime)`.

_severity: critical · confidence 0.98_

**Override `startTime` and `endTime` wrap modulo 24h when timezone offset crosses midnight**

Computing `startTime` and `endTime` via `.hour() * 60 + .minute()` after `.add(offset, "minute")` wraps around modulo 1440 whenever `offset` pushes `override.start` or `override.end` across midnight in the invitee's timezone. For example, if an organizer in UTC has an override from 14:00 to 21:00 and the invitee is in UTC+5:30 (`offset = 330`), `dayjs(override.end).utc().add(330, "minute")` becomes `02:30` the next day (`endTime = 150`), which is less than `startTime` (`1170`), causing `buildSlots` to drop the range at `if (start >= end) continue`. Compute the true UTC start/end of each override (`dayjs.utc(override.start).subtract(organizerUtcOffset, "minute")`), filter `activeOverrides` by overlap with `[startOfInviteeDay, startOfInviteeDay.endOf("day")]`, and derive `startTime` and `endTime` via `.diff(startOfInviteeDay, "minute")` clamped to `[0, 1440]`.

_severity: warning · confidence 0.92_

https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/pull/1.pr_title: SMS workflow reminder retry count tracking

golden_comments.comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

review_comments.body:
### 🥁 Not quite my tempo.

You set out to clean up failing SMS reminders, but your delete query sweeps up workflow reminders across the entire system regardless of transport method. That is not tempo; that is throwing cymbals into the crowd. Scope your database query properly before you purge reminders that do not belong to this handler.

**2** finding(s) — 1 critical, 0 warning, 1 suggestion.

**Use atomic increment for retryCount**

Do not pass `reminder.retryCount + 1` manually. If background jobs overlap, computing the next count in memory risks race conditions. Use Prisma's atomic increment operator here and in the catch handler at line 195: `retryCount: { increment: 1 }`.

_severity: suggestion · confidence 0.85_

### 🥁 Almost. Almost.

The idea is simple enough—stop hammering Twilio forever on dead SMS reminders—yet the query construction is sloppy. You dropped an unscoped `OR` branch into `deleteMany` that ignores `WorkflowMethods.SMS` and forces a full table scan on every cron tick, and you wrote `retryCount = 2` to the database just so the next cron run can delete it. Tighten the query and the update logic before this goes in.

**2** finding(s) — 0 critical, 1 warning, 1 suggestion.

**Unscoped `OR` branch deletes non-SMS reminders and forces a sequential scan**

Moving `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` inside the first `OR` branch means `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` matches `WorkflowReminder` records across all workflow methods (`EMAIL`, `WHATSAPP`, `SMS`), not just SMS. Worse, `retryCount` is unindexed on `WorkflowReminder`, so an `OR` at the top level forces Postgres to sequentially scan the entire `WorkflowReminder` table on every cron invocation. Keep `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` at the top level of `where`: `where: { method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, OR: [{ scheduledDate: { lte: dayjs().toISOString() } }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }] }`—or better yet, delete the reminder directly in the failure branch when `reminder.retryCount >= 1` instead of updating `retryCount` to 2 and waiting for the next cron run to sweep it.

### 🥁 Not quite my tempo.

You converted the service to raw SQL fragments and completely abandoned operator precedence discipline. Leaving top-level OR conditions unparenthesized is an invitation for catastrophic predicate leakage the moment a caller appends an AND clause. On top of that, you deleted the entire caching test suite instead of updating its assertions. Fix the query encapsulation and restore the test coverage.

**3** finding(s) — 2 critical, 1 warning, 0 suggestion.

#### Off the chart (couldn't anchor these to the diff)

- `packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:100` — Filter condition for eventTypeId lacks enclosing parentheses around internal OR (_critical_)
  The pushed fragment `("eventTypeId" = ${this.filters.eventTypeId}) OR ("eventParentId" = ${this.filters.eventTypeId})` lacks enclosing parentheses. When `eventTypeId` is the sole filter provided, `buildFilterConditions` returns this unparenthesized `OR` directly via `reduce`. If a caller uses `getFilterConditions()` in a composite `WHERE` clause with `AND`, the `OR` will break operator precedence. Wrap the entire expression in parentheses: `Prisma.sql`(("eventTypeId" = ${this.filters.eventTypeId}) OR ("eventParentId" = ${this.filters.eventTypeId}))``, and update the corresponding assertion in `insightsBooking.integration-test.ts`.

**Unparenthesized OR in authConditions leaks when composed with subsequent AND clauses**

When `filterConditions` is null or empty, `getBaseConditions` returns `authConditions` unwrapped. Both `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` and `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` assemble their clauses using a top-level `OR` between team bookings and individual member bookings. Because SQL evaluates `AND` before `OR`, any consumer writing `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND status = 'CONFIRMED'` will produce `(team clause) OR ((member clause) AND status = 'CONFIRMED')`, completely bypassing the caller's additional constraints for team bookings. Wrap `authConditions` (and `filterConditions`) in parentheses before returning: `return Prisma.sql`(${authConditions})`;`.

**Caching test suite was deleted instead of converted**

The service still implements `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`, but the entire `describe("Caching")` block was dropped from the integration tests rather than updating the assertions to compare against `Prisma.Sql`. Restore the caching test suite and assert that subsequent calls to `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` return the cached results.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

review_comments.body:
### 🥁 Not quite my tempo.

You tried to compose a unified OAuth credential sync layer, but you failed to verify whether any of the underlying services were playing the same tune. You wrote invalid Zod schema definitions that evaluate to stringified object literals, returned raw fetch Responses into callers expecting Axios or client SDK outputs, and wrote unparsed SafeParse wrapper structures straight into the database. Take it from the top and ensure your abstraction respects every contract it touches.

**5** finding(s) — 3 critical, 2 warning, 0 suggestion.

**Invalid Zod schema definition via computed property names**

`[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` do not create dynamic schemas in Zod. In JavaScript, both computed property names evaluate at initialization to the string literal `'[object Object]'`, meaning the second declaration overwrites the first. Because Zod strips unconfigured properties by default, this schema strips all actual fields except `access_token` and `[object Object]`. Use `z.record(z.unknown())` or `.passthrough()`, and parse or locate the expiry field explicitly.

_severity: critical · confidence 1.00_

**Persisting Zod SafeParse result object directly into credential key**

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a `SafeParseReturnType` object (`{ success: true, data: ... }`), not the parsed credential object. Storing `key` directly into `prisma.credential.update` saves `{ success: true, data: ... }` to the database. On subsequent loads, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` will fail because the credentials are nested under `data`. Save `key.data` instead: `data: { key: key.data }`.

_severity: critical · confidence 1.00_

**Mismatched return types breaking OAuth callers across integrations**

When credential sharing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response`. Callers in `GoogleCalendarService` expect an object with `.data` (`res?.data`), `zoho-bigin` and `zohocrm` expect Axios responses with `.data`, and `hubspot` expects a `HubspotToken` object. Reading `.data` or token fields directly off of a `Response` throws a `TypeError` at runtime or writes `undefined` to the database. Normalize the return type of `refreshOAuthTokens` across all integrations or adapt the responses within each service before reading token data.

_severity: critical · confidence 1.00_

**Passing credentialId instead of userId to refreshOAuthTokens**

`refreshAccessToken` passes `credentialId` as the third parameter to `refreshOAuthTokens`, which expects `userId: number | null` and forwards it as `calcomUserId`. Pass `credential.userId` to `refreshAccessToken` (or pass the full `credential` object) so that the sync endpoint receives the user's ID rather than the row ID of the credential.

_severity: warning · confidence 0.95_

**Missing HTTP method guard and case-sensitive header lookup**

The webhook handler does not verify the HTTP request method; non-POST requests will proceed to parse `req.body` and fail. Enforce the method: `if (req.method !== 'POST') return res.status(405).json({ message: 'Method not allowed' });`. Furthermore, Node.js lowercases all incoming header keys in `req.headers`, so `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || ...]` will fail if the environment variable contains uppercase characters. Normalize the lookup key with `.toLowerCase()`.

_severity: warning · confidence 0.90_

### 🥁 Not quite my tempo.

Not quite my tempo. The PR checklist literally admits tests were neither added nor run, and the diff proves it in every single adapter touched. Between a Zod schema using `[z.string().toString()]` as a computed object key, `refreshOAuthTokens` returning a `fetch` `Response` to callers expecting Axios, Gaxios, or HubSpot SDK objects, and `GoogleCalendarService` persisting a Zod `SafeParseReturnType` wrapper directly into the database, this will crash token refreshes whether credential syncing is enabled or not.

**5** finding(s) — 5 critical, 0 warning, 0 suggestion.

**Broken Zod schema definition and unconditional `refresh_token` overwrite**

In JavaScript, `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal key `"[object Object]"`, with the second overwriting the first. Because `z.object()` strips unknown keys by default, `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` strips every field except `access_token` (including expiry fields like `expires_in` and `expiry_date`), causing callers like `ZoomVideoApiAdapter` to compute `NaN` for `expiry_date`. Additionally, lines 25-27 unconditionally set `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` even when syncing is disabled, which overwrites valid stored refresh tokens in integrations like `Office365CalendarService` where `refresh_token` is optional on refresh responses. Use `.passthrough()` (or explicit expiry keys) on `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, and only supply a fallback `refresh_token` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is active.

_severity: critical · confidence 0.99_

**`parseRefreshTokenResponse` wrapper saved directly to `credential.key` and `fetch` response mismatch**

Two defects here: First, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a Zod `SafeParseSuccess` object (`{ success: true, data: ... }`), not the unwrapped credential data. Passing `key` directly to `prisma.credential.update` stores `{ success: true, data: ... }` in the database, corrupting `credential.key` so subsequent `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` calls fail. Second, when syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a standard `fetch` `Response` (which has no `.data` property), whereas `myGoogleAuth.refreshToken` returns a `GaxiosResponse` with `.data`. `res?.data` will be `undefined` and `token.access_token` will throw a `TypeError`. Parse the `fetch` JSON body consistently and pass `key.data` to `prisma.credential.update`.

_severity: critical · confidence 0.99_

**`refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch` `Response` instead of a `HubspotToken`**

When syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response`, whereas `hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken` resolves to a parsed token object (`{ accessToken, expiresIn, ... }`). Subsequent lines read `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` and `hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken` (both `undefined` on a `Response`) and write the `Response` instance into `prisma.credential.update`. The same mismatch exists in `ZohoCrmCalendarService` and `BiginCalendarService`, which expect an Axios `{ data }` response and immediately access `.data.error`. Normalize the return value of `refreshOAuthTokens` or parse the `Response` JSON before accessing token properties.

_severity: critical · confidence 0.98_

**Passing `credentialId` instead of `credential.userId` to `refreshOAuthTokens`**

`refreshOAuthTokens` expects `userId` as its third argument and sends it as `calcomUserId` to the sync endpoint, but `credentialId` (`credential.id`) is passed here instead. Pass `credential.userId` (from `biginAuth`) to `refreshAccessToken` and forward that to `refreshOAuthTokens`.

_severity: critical · confidence 0.99_

**Missing `prisma` import, missing `refreshOAuthTokens` wrapper, and stale `accessToken` used**

`prisma.credential.update` is called on line 96, but `@calcom/prisma` is not imported in this file, which will throw a `ReferenceError` at runtime. Furthermore, the token `fetch` on line 75 is not wrapped in `refreshOAuthTokens`, and `new jsforce.Connection` on line 106 still receives the old `credentialKey.access_token` instead of `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`. Import `prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`, wrap the token request in `refreshOAuthTokens`, and pass `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` to `jsforce.Connection`.

_severity: critical · confidence 0.99_

review_comments.body:
### 🥁 Not quite my tempo.

This PR attempts to fix scheduled email cancellations, but the execution is sloppy and riddled with unhandled promises and broken error recovery. You leak database records when `immediateDelete` is passed, fail to handle per-item SendGrid errors in a batch cron loop that will stall on the first hiccup, and fire unawaited asynchronous cancellations inside `forEach` loops across multiple route handlers. ### 🥁 Not quite my tempo.

You wrote an authorization check that requires a user to simultaneously be a team admin AND an owner, guaranteeing that legitimate admins are locked out. That is not just rushing; that is playing two mutually exclusive keys and praying the chord resolves itself. Couple that with redundant database roundtrips, foreign calendar credentials used for event updates, and an unfiltered email list passed to the notification pipeline, and this whole movement falls apart. Clean it up.

**4** finding(s) — 1 critical, 3 warning, 0 suggestion.

**Logical AND prevents team admins and owners from adding guests**

The variable is named `isTeamAdminOrOwner`, but you joined the predicates with `&&`. In Cal.com, membership roles are distinct: a user is not simultaneously an `ADMIN` and an `OWNER`. Joining them with `&&` ensures this check evaluates to `false` for every team admin or owner. Replace `&&` with `||`.

_severity: critical · confidence 1.00_

**Redundant query with unsafe zero ID fallback on nullable booking.userId**

`booking.user` is already fetched on lines 35–41. Querying `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow` again is redundant. More critically, `booking.userId` is nullable; passing `booking.userId || 0` will cause `findFirstOrThrow` to throw a `NotFoundError` and crash the request with a 500 when `booking.userId` is `null`. Reuse `booking.user` instead of querying the database a second time.

_severity: warning · confidence 0.95_

**Caller credentials used instead of booking host credentials for calendar sync**

`EventManager` is instantiated using `ctx.user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. If a team admin or attendee invokes this mutation, `ctx.user` is not the host whose calendar holds the event. Calendar integrations will fail when attempting to update third-party calendar entries using credentials that do not own the calendar event. Initialize `EventManager` using the booking host (`booking.user`) and their credentials.

_severity: warning · confidence 0.90_

**Raw guest input passed to email sender instead of deduplicated list**

`sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives raw `input.guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`. If the input contained an existing attendee, `sendAddGuestsEmails` checks `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` and incorrectly sends them `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (a new booking confirmation) rather than `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Pass `uniqueGuests.map((g) => g.email)` instead. Additionally, do not swallow mailer failures with `console.log`; use `@calcom/lib/logger`.

### 🥁 Not quite my tempo.

You rushed through authentication and handed me a security bypass. If an attacker passes a dummy TOTP code alongside a backup code, password verification is skipped entirely and the account is breached. On top of that, backup code comparison is strictly case-sensitive against hex values, and your modal navigation button submits the form. Start from measure one and get the fundamentals down.

**4** finding(s) — 1 critical, 2 warning, 1 suggestion.

**Password verification bypass when backupCode is provided with a dummy totpCode**

Line 120 skips `verifyPassword` whenever `credentials.totpCode` is truthy (`if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)`). Because line 131 checks `credentials.backupCode` first, an attacker supplying a victim's email, any non-empty string for `totpCode`, and a valid `backupCode` will bypass both password verification and TOTP verification, gaining full access without the password. Ensure that `credentials.password` is verified when authenticating with a backup code: `if (user.password && (!credentials.totpCode || credentials.backupCode))`.

_severity: critical · confidence 0.95_

**Backup code comparison is case-sensitive and fails on untrimmed input**

Backup codes are generated via `crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`, producing lowercase hex strings. However, `BackupCode.tsx` displays the placeholder `XXXXX-XXXXX`, prompting users to enter uppercase letters. Comparing via `backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` without case normalization or trimming causes valid uppercase or copy-pasted codes to be rejected. Normalize the input using `credentials.backupCode.trim().toLowerCase().replaceAll("-", "")`. Apply the same fix in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`.

**Navigation button missing type="button" triggers form submission**

The 'Lost access' / 'Go back' `<Button>` is rendered inside `<Form>` without `type="button"`. In HTML, buttons inside a form default to `type="submit"`. Clicking this button triggers form validation and submission rather than just toggling the modal view. Add `type="button"` to the `<Button>` component.

_severity: warning · confidence 0.95_

review_comments.body:
### 🥁 Not quite my tempo.

This PR attempts to convert destination calendars into arrays for collective scheduling, but it is riddled with basic runtime hazards and carelessness. We have an unhandled TypeError waiting to crash bookings on Google Meet, circular fallback logic in Google Calendar, silent data loss for collective host calendars, and an unrelated file modified with an inverted boolean. Rehearse this until it actually works.

**4** finding(s) — 2 critical, 2 warning, 0 suggestion.

**Unhandled TypeError accessing properties of undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar**

When `evt.destinationCalendar` is empty (`[]`) or undefined, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` resolves to `undefined`. Accessing `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws an uncaught `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` and aborts event creation. Use optional chaining: `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar")`.

_severity: critical · confidence 0.95_

**Inverted billing condition breaks organization slug assignment in unrelated file**

This file is completely unrelated to destination calendars. Furthermore, replacing `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` with `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}` breaks org creation when team billing is disabled (the slug is omitted entirely) and sets both `slug` and `requestedSlug` when billing is enabled. Revert these modifications.

_severity: critical · confidence 0.95_

**Initializing destinationCalendar to null silently drops collective hosts' calendars**

When neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists, `destinationCalendar` is set to `null`. On line 1078, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` optional-chains on `null` and silently fails, discarding every secondary host's destination calendar. Default to an empty array instead: `destinationCalendar: eventType.destinationCalendar ? [eventType.destinationCalendar] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [organizerUser.destinationCalendar] : []`.

_severity: warning · confidence 0.90_

**Circular fallback searches for falsy externalCalendarId**

In `updateEvent` (line 256) and `deleteEvent` (line 315), the fallback branch evaluates `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. If `externalCalendarId` is falsy (which is the only reason the fallback executes), searching for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` will compare against `undefined` or `null` and will never match. Fall back to `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` instead.

_severity: warning · confidence 0.90_

### 🥁 Not quite my tempo.

Not quite my tempo. This PR claims to support collective hosts across any calendar app, yet only Google Calendar actually looks up the destination calendar by credentialId while Office 365, Lark, and CalDAV blindly grab index 0—the primary organizer's calendar. Worse, you introduced an unguarded property access on an undefined destination calendar, wiped out credentialId on video booking references, wrote a dead fallback comparison in Google Calendar's update/delete methods, and flipped a billing flag in an unrelated organization handler.

**7** finding(s) — 4 critical, 3 warning, 0 suggestion.

**Unguarded property access on mainHostDestinationCalendar crashes when destinationCalendar is empty or null**

When `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, `undefined`, or `[]`, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined`. Removing the optional chaining before `.integration` causes a `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` whenever `evt.location === MeetLocationType` and the user has no destination calendar set. Restore optional chaining: `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

_severity: critical · confidence 0.99_

**Video booking references lose their credentialId on creation**

Previously this line was `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId`. By changing the false branch to `undefined`, dedicated video results (`!isCalendarType`) no longer persist their `credentialId` on `BookingReference`. Downstream handlers like `handleCancelBooking` and `handleSeatedEventCancellation` rely on `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` to delete or update the video meeting. Use `credentialId: result.credentialId`.

_severity: critical · confidence 0.96_

**Non-Google calendar services always use the primary host's destinationCalendar instead of matching credentialId**

In `Calendar.d.ts` and `CalendarManager.ts`, `createEvent` now receives `credentialId: number`, and `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent` uses it to find the matching entry in `event.destinationCalendar`. However, `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` (as well as `LarkCalendarService.createEvent` at line 128 and `BaseCalendarService.createEvent` at line 156) ignores `credentialId` and destructures the first element `[mainHostDestinationCalendar]`. In a collective booking, `event.destinationCalendar[0]` belongs to the primary organizer, so secondary hosts on Office 365, Lark, or CalDAV will query their own account using the primary host's `externalId` and fail. Accept `credentialId: number` in `createEvent` across these services and select `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId) ?? mainHostDestinationCalendar`.

_severity: critical · confidence 0.95_

**Unrelated change inverts IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition for organization slug**

This file is unrelated to `destinationCalendar`, and changing `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` inverts the boolean condition. When team billing is disabled, `slug` will no longer be set on organization creation; when team billing is enabled, `slug` will be set prematurely alongside `metadata.requestedSlug`. Revert the changes to this file.

_severity: critical · confidence 0.98_

**Fallback calendar lookup in updateEvent and deleteEvent compares against a falsy externalCalendarId**

In both `updateEvent` (line 256) and `deleteEvent` (line 317), the false branch of `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : ...` only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (`null`, `undefined`, or `""`). Searching `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` in that branch looks for a calendar whose `externalId` is falsy, which will never match a valid `DestinationCalendar` and can only evaluate to `undefined`. Fall back to `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` (or `"primary"` in `updateEvent`, and also ensure `selectedCalendar || "primary"` is passed to `calendar.events.patch` on line 170).

_severity: warning · confidence 0.96_

**Collective hosts' destination calendars are silently dropped if the organizer has no destinationCalendar**

On lines 1063-1067, `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` is set. Consequently, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` on line 1078 becomes a no-op due to optional chaining on `null`, discarding all secondary hosts' destination calendars. Initialize `destinationCalendar` to `[]` instead of `null` (consistent with the other handlers in this PR).

_severity: warning · confidence 0.95_

**Missing null guard on credential before calling updateEvent and swallowed error log**

Unlike `createAllCalendarEvents` (line 369), `updateAllCalendarEvents` calls `updateEvent(credential, ...)` on line 542 without checking if `credential` is still `undefined` after the database lookup, which will throw a `TypeError` inside `updateEvent` when reading `credential.appName`. Additionally, `console.error(message)` was removed in the `catch` block at line 592, leaving `message` unused and silencing unexpected errors. Guard `updateEvent` with `if (credential)` and restore logging in the `catch` block.

_severity: warning · confidence 0.93_

https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/pull/8.pr_title: Async import of the appStore packages

golden_comments.comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

review_comments.body:
### 🥁 Almost. Almost.

You set out to introduce async imports, but you evaluated every single dynamic import immediately inside an object literal. That is not lazy loading; it is eager evaluation with extra steps. On top of that, you slapped async keywords onto forEach callbacks and left critical deletions floating unawaited. Tighten the timing.

**3** finding(s) — 0 critical, 3 warning, 0 suggestion.

**Eager dynamic imports defeat lazy loading**

Directly calling import("./applecalendar") in the object literal executes the dynamic import immediately when packages/app-store/index.ts is evaluated. All 28 app bundles are triggered concurrently on boot, defeating the entire purpose of code splitting. Define getters (for example: get applecalendar() { return import("./applecalendar"); }) or wrap the object in a Proxy so that modules are loaded only when accessed, without breaking the await appStore[appName] caller syntax.

_severity: warning · confidence 0.95_

**Async forEach callback leaves deletions unawaited**

Array.prototype.forEach ignores the promise returned by an async callback. The calendar and video meeting deletions run detached in the background while requestReschedule immediately advances to send emails and return. Any error thrown inside becomes an unhandled promise rejection. Replace forEach with await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... })).

_severity: warning · confidence 0.95_

**Async callback escapes try-catch in forEach**

Making the forEach callback async renders the surrounding try-catch block completely useless; forEach returns undefined synchronously, and rejections inside the callback will not be caught. Use await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... })) inside the try block to ensure deletions settle before emails are dispatched.

_severity: warning · confidence 0.95_

### 🥁 Not quite my tempo.

Not quite my tempo. The entire premise of this pull request is lazy, asynchronous loading of `appStore` packages, yet `packages/app-store/index.ts` fires every single `import()` eagerly at module initialization time. Worse, the codebase is now littered with `forEach(async ...)` anti-patterns that break `try/catch` error handling and leave `apiDeletes` empty when `Promise.all` runs. Fix the fundamentals before bringing this back on stage.

**5** finding(s) — 2 critical, 3 warning, 0 suggestion.

**Dynamic `import()` calls in object literal execute eagerly on module load**

Assigning `import("./...")` directly as property values in the `appStore` object literal evaluates all 28 dynamic imports immediately when `@calcom/app-store` is imported, completely defeating lazy on-demand loading and risking unhandled promise rejections if any unused integration fails to load. Wrap each import in a getter (e.g., `get applecalendar() { return import("./applecalendar"); }`) so `await appStore[appName]` only loads the requested module on access, or make each entry a factory function (`applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) and invoke it at the call sites.

_severity: critical · confidence 0.99_

**Unawaited `forEach(async ...)` prevents recurring calendar deletions from being awaited**

`Array.prototype.forEach` does not await `async` callbacks. When `await getCalendar(credential)` suspends execution, control flows past this block and `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` runs before `apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent)` is ever reached. Replace `.forEach(async (credential) => ...)` with a `for...of` loop (as done in the `else` branch on lines 477-483) and push the `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` promises into `apiDeletes`.

_severity: critical · confidence 0.96_

**`forEach(async ...)` inside `try/catch` leaks unhandled promise rejections**

`bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` returns `undefined` immediately without awaiting the async callback. Any rejection from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent`, or `deleteMeeting` will bypass the surrounding `try/catch` block as an unhandled promise rejection, and `Reschedule` will return before deletions finish. Replace `forEach` with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }))`.

_severity: warning · confidence 0.95_

**`forEach(async ...)` inside `try/catch` leaks unhandled promise rejections**

Just as in `vital/lib/reschedule.ts`, passing an `async` callback to `forEach` inside a `try/catch` block means promise rejections from `await getCalendar(...)`, `deleteEvent`, or `deleteMeeting` are never caught or awaited. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }))` instead.

_severity: warning · confidence 0.95_

**Floating promises in `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)`**

`forEach` discards the promises returned by the `async` callback, so `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent`, and `deleteMeeting` run as detached background tasks that can reject unhandled or be cut short when the mutation resolves. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }))` so the deletions complete before the mutation finishes.

_severity: warning · confidence 0.93_
